Convert entity patterns of phrases to a quanteda dictionary

Source: R/as.dictionary.R
as.dictionary.spacyr_entity_patterns.Rd

A method of quanteda::as.dictionary() for the entity patterns that as_entity_patterns() makes, when all of them are phrases: each label becomes a key, and the phrases with that label become its values. It needs the quanteda package, and is available when quanteda is loaded.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'spacyr_entity_patterns'
as.dictionary(x, ...)

Arguments

x

a spacyr_entity_patterns object, as as_entity_patterns() or entity_patterns_read() returns, whose patterns are all phrases

...

not used; any argument given here is an error

Value

A quanteda dictionary with one key for each label of x, in the order in which the labels first occur. Its values are the different phrases with that label, in the case in which they are written.

Details

A dictionary holds words and phrases, so x can hold only phrases. Token patterns have no counterpart in a dictionary: when x has any, the conversion stops with an error that names their labels.

A dictionary has less than the entity patterns have, so the conversion keeps the different pairs of a label and a phrase, and nothing else:

  • The id of a pattern is dropped.

  • So is case_insensitive. A dictionary does not say how its values are matched: that is set where it is used, as by case_insensitive in quanteda::tokens_lookup() or in as_entity_patterns().

  • quanteda::dictionary() removes the whitespace at the start and the end of a value, and a phrase that occurs more than once under a label is kept once.

  • The values are grouped by key, so their order is not the order of the patterns when the patterns of a label are not next to each other.

quanteda reads * and ? in a dictionary value as wildcards, since its default is valuetype = "glob", while in a phrase of an entity pattern they are those characters themselves. The conversion gives a warning when a phrase has one. To match such values as they are written, use valuetype = "fixed", as in quanteda::tokens_lookup(x, dictionary, valuetype = "fixed").

An object with no patterns gives a dictionary with no keys, which as_entity_patterns() makes into no patterns again. quanteda takes such a dictionary in quanteda::kwic() and quanteda::dfm_lookup(), but quanteda::tokens_lookup() stops with an error for it (in quanteda 4.5.1), so check length() of the dictionary first where it can be empty.

To make entity patterns of the dictionary again, with the phrases as they are written and matched in their own case, use as_entity_patterns(d, valuetype = "fixed", case_insensitive = FALSE). Without those arguments, as_entity_patterns() reads the values of a dictionary as quanteda does: as globs, matched in any case.

See also

as_entity_patterns(), quanteda::dictionary(), quanteda::tokens_lookup()

Examples

pat <- as_entity_patterns(c(ORG = "Acme Widgets", ORG = "Globex",
                            GPE = "New York"))
d <- quanteda::as.dictionary(pat)
d
#> Dictionary object with 2 key entries.
#> - [ORG]:
#>   - Acme Widgets, Globex
#> - [GPE]:
#>   - New York

# and back, as phrases matched in their own case
as_entity_patterns(d, valuetype = "fixed", case_insensitive = FALSE)
#> Entity patterns: 3 patterns (ORG: 2, GPE: 1)
#>   ORG  "Acme Widgets"
#>   ORG  "Globex"
#>   GPE  "New York"
